newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-JACQUET'S EXPERIMENTS SHOW FRANCE IN GOOD LIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JACQUET'S EXPERIMENTS SHOW FRANCE IN GOOD LIGHT.

text.p: French coach Aime Jacquet, experimenting with his squad before France hosts the World Cup next year, could be forgiven for giving himself a small pat on the back on Thursday.

While he will not allow himself a second to rest on his laurels, France's 2-1 come-from-behind win over a strong Dutch side on Wednesday night, hints that he is going along the right lines in building a squad capable of mounting a serious challenge in the battle for the world title.

France recovered from a third minute goal scored by Dennis Bergkamp and won with two in the last 16 minutes from substitutes Patrice Loko and Robert Pires, and that gave Jacquet the chance for a small smile.
"This victory will really help our World Cup preparations," he said on Thursday.
Bergkamp's early goal meant that Jacquet had to change his game plan.
He had wanted to play with three containing central midfielders and an arrowhead attack of two deep lying forwards and one striker.

But after 32 minutes Metz wing-back Pires replaced Sampdoria's Pierre Laigle, one of the three defensive midfielders alongside Christian Karembeu and debutant Patrick Vieira, playing against Bergkamp, his Arsenal team mate .
The fast running Dutch powered through the midfield in the early stages with no-one to counter the attacking runs of Michael Reiziger on the French left flank.
"I had to intervene very quickly, change something to restore the team's stability," Jacquet said.
"In view of that, I think it was a good evening of football... The match was rich in lessons for the future."

Jacquet, having lost a three-year 30-match unbeaten run in Denmark in December, laid out his plans for the first half of 1997 that included experimenting with three different game plans before June's World Cup warm-up tournament against Brazil, England and Italy.
His experiment on Wednesday, following France's 2-0 away win over Portugal last month hints that he is on the right lines.
Barcelona defender Laurent Blanc, standing in as captain for the injured Didier Deschamps, said the Dutch were superior on a technical level in the first half.
"When we placed the combat on a physical level they gradually let their grip go," Blanc said.
"But if athletically we created a real difference, we also showed real aptitudes in the game and that's encouraging for the future."
France hustled the Dutch off their game, in which their three-man movements are extremely effective and which has produced 13 goals in three successive World Cup qualifying victories.

Goalkeeper Bernard Lama, whose return after injury along with that of Athletic Bilbao left back Bixente Lizarazu saw Jacquet restore his full Euro 96 defence, said the match showed France's will to progress.
"We took a half to find our rhythm and above all any fault in the Dutch system. We had to be more direct, push them back into their half. That's what we managed to do with intelligence," he said.
Having been forced to make an early change, Jacquet is still keen to experiment to the full with the formation that took the field on Wednesday.
He said he hopes to do this against Sweden at home on April 2 as he seeks to make his squad versatile for a tournament of several matches in quick succession.
